asian_option_pricer.text:
`basket_option_pricer` prices an option on a weighted sum of several correlated assets at maturity, so it answers "what is this basket option worth, given each asset's `spots`, `sigmas`, `weights` and the `correlation` matrix?" `asian_option_pricer` prices an option on a single underlying's arithmetic average over time, so it answers "what is this averaging option worth on one asset?" Both use Monte Carlo and discount the expected payoff at the risk-free `rate`.

The basket function takes per-asset inputs and a strike on the weighted basket. The Asian function takes a single `spot` and `sigma`, plus `n_steps` for how many observation points enter the average. It also offers `div_yield` and a `qmc` option. For sensitivities, `greeks` in the basket pricer gives per-asset delta, gamma and vega (diagonal only) plus scalar theta and rho. In the Asian pricer it gives delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho.

explain.text: The Basket Option Pricer (`basket_option_pricer`) prices an option on a weighted basket of assets using Monte Carlo simulation. It simulates correlated terminal prices for each asset from `spots`, `sigmas` and a `correlation` matrix, forms the basket with `weights`, and discounts the average payoff against `strike` at the risk-free `rate`. You choose a `call` or `put` via `option_type`, and set the number of paths with `n_simulations`. Setting `greeks` to true also returns per-asset delta, gamma and vega, plus theta and rho, by bump-and-reprice.

when.text:
Use the Basket Option Pricer (`basket_option_pricer`) when you need a price for an option written on a weighted sum of several assets rather than on one asset.

- You have a strike on the weighted basket, and can supply per-asset `spots`, `weights` and `sigmas`, plus a `correlation` matrix.
- Correlation between the assets matters to your payoff, since pyvar simulates correlated paths through Monte Carlo.
- You want either a call or a put, set with `option_type`.
- You also want per-asset delta, gamma and vega, plus theta and rho, by setting `greeks` to true. Delta, gamma and vega are diagonal only, with no cross-asset terms.
- For a different payoff, `rainbow_option_pricer` is listed as pricing best-of / worst-of options via Monte Carlo.
